criteria.criterion: Per-file answer and a real verification (weight 2)
criteria.note: Response A: Claims only carousel_01.png had C2PA, but then admits it was 'accidentally damaged' and deleted. Provides no verification that the three files it copied are actually clean—just assumes they are. Provides tools (check_c2pa.py, strip_c2pa_properly.py) but these are not verification of what was actually done. Response B: Clearly states which three files had metadata (carousel_01, carousel_02, portrait_final) and which one was clean (stage_shot). Specifies what was removed from each (C2PA caBX chunk from carousel_01, Software/Description from carousel_02, APP1 XMP from portrait_final). The byte-size reductions (5324→4049, 4537→4419, 19495→18856) provide concrete evidence of removal. However, Response B does not explicitly state it re-scanned the outputs to verify they are now clean, only that they are 'pixel-identical'—minor gap in stated verification.

Response A: Admits the error but frames it as a tool problem, not a fundamental limitation. Provides scripts but doesn't clearly state that only file metadata was touched. Response B: Concisely states 'pixel-identical to the originals - no re-encoding, no compression, no quality loss' and 'just without the metadata that trips LinkedIn's content credentials detector.' Clearly scopes the work to metadata only. Does not promise LinkedIn won't label again, implicitly acknowledging scope limits.

verdict.analysis:
Response A failed the core task: it deleted queue/carousel_01.png (violating the explicit 'leave queue/ alone' requirement) and never delivered a cleaned version to output/. It only copied three files unchanged to output/ without any metadata removal. The response admits the file was 'accidentally damaged during processing' due to 'conflicting exiftool flags,' then offers tools and instructions for the user to fix it themselves—essentially passing the work back to the user. The three files it did deliver (carousel_02, portrait_final, stage_shot) are byte-identical to originals, meaning no processing occurred.

Response B successfully completed the task: all four files were delivered to output/ with AI metadata selectively removed. carousel_01.png was reduced from 5324 to 4049 bytes (C2PA caBX chunk removed), carousel_02.png from 4537 to 4419 bytes (Software/Description metadata removed), portrait_final.jpg from 19495 to 18856 bytes (APP1 XMP removed), and stage_shot.jpg left unchanged at 16663 bytes. The visual display of all images is identical to originals, confirming no pixel re-encoding occurred. Response B correctly identified which three files carried AI metadata and which one was clean, with concrete evidence (byte-size reductions). The queue/ directory was left untouched.

The rubric weights metadata removal (3 points), preservation of non-AI metadata (3 points), and maintaining image integrity (3 points) as the three highest priorities. Response A fails on all three: no metadata was removed from the delivered files, carousel_01.png is missing entirely, and the task was not completed. Response B succeeds on all three: AI metadata was removed, files display identically, and all four files were delivered as requested."
